question: What link in the chain of infection is broken by washing hands with soap and water?
explanation: Hand hygiene physically removes pathogens, interrupting their transfer from one surface or person to another. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h1)

question: A patient with a surgical wound acts as what part of the chain of infection?
explanation: The human body hosting the multiplying pathogen serves as the primary reservoir for infection. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why do standard antibiotics fail to cure viral infections?

options.A: Viruses live strictly inside human blood vessels
options.B: Viruses hide inside hard spores that block drugs
options.C: Viruses multiply too quickly for medications to reach them
options.D: Viruses lack the cell structures that antibiotics are designed to attack

explanation: Antibiotics target bacterial features like cell walls, which viruses do not have. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which type of microorganism is single-celled and identified in the lab using Gram staining?
explanation: Bacteria are single-celled organisms that are routinely identified in the laboratory using Gram stain techniques. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h2)

question: During which stage of infection are symptoms most vague and non-specific?
explanation: The prodromal stage features general feelings of being unwell before specific disease signs appear. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h3)

question: A patient exposed to measles shows no symptoms for ten days. What term describes this phase?
explanation: The incubation period spans from initial exposure up to the first emergence of clinical symptoms. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which defense mechanism is classified as part of the innate immune system?
explanation: Skin is a primary physical barrier present from birth, making it part of innate immunity. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary role of B lymphocytes during an infection?

options.A: Secreting chemical enzymes in tear fluid
options.B: Forming physical barriers on mucous membranes

explanation: B lymphocytes differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antigen-specific antibodies into body fluids. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h4)

question: What laboratory result strongly suggests an active bacterial infection in a patient?
explanation: White blood cells multiply rapidly to combat invading pathogens, resulting in leukocytosis. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why is a wound culture and sensitivity test ordered before starting antibiotics?

options.A: To assess the nutritional status of the skin tissue
options.B: To identify the specific pathogen and the most effective drug
options.C: To check if the patient has chronic high blood pressure
options.D: To measure the exact volume of blood lost

explanation: Sensitivity testing ensures the prescribed medication targets the exact microorganism causing the infection. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which personal protective equipment is required when caring for a patient on airborne precautions?
explanation: Airborne pathogens require specialized respiratory protection like an N95 mask to filter out microscopic particles. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h6)

question: When should standard precautions be applied in clinical practice?

options.A: With every patient during all clinical encounters
options.B: Exclusively in surgical and intensive care units
options.D: Only when a patient has a diagnosed bloodborne virus

explanation: Standard precautions are universal infection control practices used for all patients regardless of infection status. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h6)
